subject: brain scan
title: Doctors Scanned a Man's Head and Found It Was Mostly Fluid. He Was Fine

scenes.text: Doctors scanned a man's head and found mostly fluid.
He was 44, a French civil servant with two children. He'd come in because his left leg felt weak.
The scans showed a huge fluid-filled space inside his skull. His brain was pressed into a thin layer around the edge.
He'd been treated for fluid on the brain as a baby. It had slowly built up again.
His IQ tested at 75: below average, but he held a job and raised a family.
All of it on a thin sheet of brain.

description:
In 2007, doctors in Marseille scanned a 44-year-old man's head and found it was mostly fluid.
The man, a married civil servant with two children, came to hospital with mild weakness in his left leg. Scans showed hugely enlarged fluid-filled ventricles and only a thin mantle of brain tissue around them. He had been treated with a shunt for hydrocephalus at six months old and again at 14. Tests gave him an IQ of 75 (verbal 84, performance 70), and he lived an ordinary life. After a new shunt was fitted, his leg recovered within weeks; his scans did not change. The case was published in The Lancet by Lionel Feuillet and colleagues as 'Brain of a white-collar worker'.
What does that say about how much brain we need? Comment below.
first_comment: After treatment his leg recovered within weeks, and a later scan showed his brain had not changed size. What does that say about how much brain we need?
